chapters.title: Engineering medical research and the cost of repetition
Questioning the categories used for human hearing
High-throughput experiments and the Recursion example
Building a research operating system with Rust, Julia and C++
Curiosity, engineering and the closing message

existingSummary: Zak Allal explains how cheaper, repeatable experiments can change scientific research. Drawing on his work with hearing data, he describes using supercomputers, Rust, Julia and C++ to build a clinical research operating system, challenge existing categories and develop a proposed five-dimensional hearing atlas. He closes with the role of curiosity, careful engineering and knowledge across disciplines.
